questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop, no matter what.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross safely. Stay alert at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
Snow tires help your vehicle grip the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other dangerous conditions. Winter driving is hard and needs extra care. Check antifreeze and washer fluid. Snow tires help your car stay on slippery roads.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." This means:

options.text: The 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The 35 mph speed limit starts at the next sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down.
Reduce speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A "Reduced speed" sign tells you to slow down. The new speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: Always use your turn signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when changing lanes, parking, or pulling into traffic.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to warn the bicyclist.
Drive in the bike lane to pass.
Slow down and give them plenty of space.
Speed ahead to get in front of them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Slow down when passing a bicyclist. Give them as much room as possible. Bicyclists have little protection, and passing too fast can knock them off course.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Have large blind spots.
Can stop faster than cars.
Need the same space to turn as cars.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the back. Stay out of these areas. Trucks need more room to turn and stop than cars because they are larger and heavier.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street without its lights or siren on. You should:

options.text: Drive normally.
Stop quickly.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down, move right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is not using its siren or flashing lights, you do not need to move. Drive normally.

questions.question: Before turning left, you must:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Let oncoming traffic pass first.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for the other traffic light to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let oncoming traffic pass first.
questions.explanation: When turning left, give the right-of-way to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines on the road mean:

options.text: Both directions can pass.
No passing is allowed.
Passing is okay at the top of a hill.
Passing is okay during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing is allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass.

questions.question: You meet an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the other vehicle at least half of the road.
Force the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the other vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, let oncoming vehicles use at least half of the road. Both drivers need space to pass safely.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving. You have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the intersection is dangerous. Always treat it like a stop sign and come to a complete stop.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, let other traffic pass first, and match the speed of traffic on the freeway.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must let you in.
Drive slowly while you check the traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other traffic pass first, and match the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: Signal before you merge. Let other traffic pass first. Match the speed of traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What should you do when crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates while in traffic?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to look for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks completely without stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto the tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely. Never try to pass other vehicles at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body get rid of in one hour?

options.text: Three alcoholic drinks.
One alcoholic drink.
Two alcoholic drinks.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink.
questions.explanation: Your body processes about one drink per hour. But many things affect how impaired you become, including how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your weight, how much you have eaten, and your overall health.

questions.question: Your wheels drop onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: Slow down without braking hard. Turn back onto the road carefully. Watch for other traffic when you re-enter the road.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights and fog lights if you have them. High beams bounce off fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Which of these is a sign of a drunk driver?

options.text: Weaving between lanes.
Driving slower than normal traffic.
Making quick and sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving too slowly, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: You are driving at night and see another vehicle coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam.
On low beam.
Off. Use parking lights instead.
On either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: On low beam.
questions.explanation: Always use low beam headlights when another vehicle is coming toward you or when you are following another vehicle at night.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. What steps should you take to merge safely?

options.text: Use your mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the entrance ramp to speed up and match freeway traffic.
Let traffic on the freeway pass first.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to match freeway speed. Let freeway traffic pass first. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The safe speed limit for a residential area.
The safe speed for a highway exit.
The safe speed for a highway entrance.
The safe speed for a construction zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The safe speed for a highway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the safe speed for a highway exit. In this example, the safe speed is 30 mph.
